extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal education funds (elementary, secondary, and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and complying with §106.44(c) notification requirements and related provisions of the final Title IX regulations, including employee reporting duties, confidential-employee rules, training, and Title IX Coordinator responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification trigger — "reasonably may constitute sex discrimination"
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee must notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that "reasonably" may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees are not required to determine whether the conduct meets every aspect of the regulation's definition of sex discrimination (including hostile environment). Rather, an employee must respond to conduct or information that could reasonably meet that definition. If an employee directly witnesses conduct under the recipient's program or activity that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the employee is considered to have "information" and must report it or provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and complaint-making information to the person subjected to the conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee training on scope and notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train all employees on the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination under Title IX, including sex-based harassment, and on applicable notification requirements (see §106.8(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training helps employees recognize when information reported to them reasonably may constitute sex discrimination so they know when to notify. The Department simplified the notification framework to make implementation and training easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee exemption and disclosure duties (§106.44(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees are exempt from the obligation to notify the Title IX Coordinator but must explain their confidential status and circumstances when they are not required to notify (§106.44(d)(2)). Recipients must notify participants how to contact confidential employees (§106.44(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A confidential employee must explain to any person who informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination the employee's confidential status, how to contact the Title IX Coordinator, and that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer supportive measures or initiate an informal resolution or investigation. This supports complainant autonomy while enabling appropriate responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: PII nondisclosure protections (§106.44(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations generally prohibit disclosure of personally identifiable information obtained in complying with this part, except in limited circumstances (e.g., to a parent/guardian or authorized legal representative or as necessary to carry out the purposes of 34 CFR part 106).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must protect personal information of all students, including LGBTQI+ students and pregnant students. §106.44(j) permits disclosures only in limited, specified circumstances; see §106.44(j)(3) for disclosures necessary to carry out Title IX purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: K–12 rule: all non-confidential employees must notify (§106.44(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For elementary and secondary schools, all employees who are not confidential employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The K–12 rule recognizes teachers/administrators' supervisory roles and aligns with state child-abuse mandatory reporting duties. Determinations account for context including parties' ages; required training enables employees to exercise judgment appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postsecondary two-category approach (§106.44(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients other than elementary/secondary schools must distinguish two categories of non-confidential employees: Category 1 (authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising) and Category 2 (all other non-confidential employees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category 1 employees must notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. Category 2 employees must either notify the Title IX Coordinator or provide the Title IX Coordinator's contact information and complaint-making information to the person who reports; the recipient may decide which of these two actions Category 2 employees must take or leave the decision to employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: No distinction based on whether reporter is student or employee
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations do not differentiate notification obligations based on whether the person providing information is a student or an employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed distinctions between students and employees to simplify requirements so employees know what they must do in any circumstance rather than altering actions based on reporter status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notice of nondiscrimination and how to report (§106.8(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide a notice of nondiscrimination that includes information on how to report conduct that may constitute sex discrimination and how to make a complaint, and how to locate nondiscrimination policies and grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may include information about which employees have notification duties and about confidential employees in the notice of nondiscrimination. The Department declined to require posting of full reporting protocols online, preferring flexibility in how recipients meet notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duties after notification (§106.44(f),(g),(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notification, the Title IX Coordinator must offer and, if accepted, coordinate supportive measures (§106.44(g)), notify the complainant (or reporting individual if complainant unknown) of grievance procedures (§106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46) and the informal resolution process (§106.44(k)); in limited circumstances the Coordinator may initiate a complaint (§106.44(f)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a complainant declines to initiate grievance procedures, the Coordinator must offer supportive measures. A complainant's request not to proceed is a factor the Coordinator must consider before initiating a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant autonomy maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants retain autonomy over whether to make a complaint; the Title IX Coordinator must consider complainant wishes when deciding whether to initiate a complaint and supportive measures are available regardless of filing a grievance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only in very limited circumstances may a Coordinator initiate a complaint over a complainant's wishes; §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A(1)) requires considering a complainant's request not to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process protections for respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification to the Title IX Coordinator does not inherently impair a respondent's due process rights; not all reports lead to investigations or grievance procedures, and grievance procedures (§106.45, §106.46) are designed to provide a fair process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department maintains that employees should only act on information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, and notification can lead to processes that protect respondents' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment and religious-belief considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification requirements are not intended to chill protected speech; academic discourse generally would not meet the threshold for notification. Individual religious beliefs do not excuse employees from recipient-level notification obligations; Title IX regulations do not restrict First Amendment rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to exempt disclosures made in applications, interviews, or academic assignments from notification where they provide information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination. Religious liberty issues are addressed elsewhere (§106.2 discussion), and the statute permits religious-institution exemptions but not individual-employee exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient implementation flexibility and burden considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may have more extensive Title IX Coordinator duties; recipients may designate multiple Title IX Coordinators and delegate tasks but must designate one Coordinator to retain ultimate oversight (§106.8(a)(2)). The Department considered compliance costs in the Regulatory Impact Analysis and concluded benefits justify the burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department streamlined §106.44(c) to reduce complexity and training burden. Recipients have discretion in some Category 2 choices and in how to meet notice requirements (e.g., whether to post protocols online).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with law enforcement and other mandates
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX regulations do not control when law enforcement is involved; law enforcement interactions are governed by state/local/federal laws separate from Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title IX implements protections the Department has authority to enforce; recipients must coordinate Title IX responsibilities consistent with other legal obligations regarding law enforcement involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity about confidential resources supports complainant autonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide clarity regarding confidential employees and resources so complainants can make informed decisions about disclosure and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear communication about confidential employees (who will not trigger mandatory reporting) and mandatory reporters allows complainants to seek support while enabling the institution to address sex discrimination consistent with complainant preferences.
